$comment: requires_bootstrap is 0.160.0, the first bootstrap that holds a plugin venv at the highest released version of a first-party package its pyproject requires (the released-target venv stamp) and revokes undeclared bootstrap-written .pth links. The venv needs that because it installs katsoft-llm-kit (>=1.3,<2), whose llm_kit.adapters.codex_command is what the bootstrap_lib.codex alias resolves to, so the venv's llm_kit is the wheel and never a stale link. The call shapes are older: shipped skill text launches scripts as "${BOOTSTRAP_PYTHON:?requires bootstrap >= 0.120.0}", which only bootstrap 0.120.0's SessionStart hook exports. The bootstrap_lib edges (execution_event, interrupt_contract; model_declaration is named only in docs) are degrade-guarded at runtime in execution/events.py and execution/interrupts.py, which probe for absent, too-old or stale and report instead of requiring a newer bootstrap, so they do not raise the floor above it. content-pipeline-kit's llm/ package consumes the llm_scripting_kit shared lib for the live (openrouter / model-endpoint / claude-cli / codex-cli / opencode-cli) backends, so the owner plugin plugins-kit:llm-scripting-kit must be installed for that lib to be published to _shared_libs. Declaring it install: auto makes opting into content-pipeline-kit pull its dependency automatically -- dependency semantics, distinct from the action-triggered opt-in pattern (bootstrap skill, references/action-triggered-install.md). bootstrap_lib is linked in TRANSITIVELY: CodexCliBackend imports bootstrap_lib.codex (the argv single source of truth) lazily, at dispatch time rather than import time, so without this entry the codex path imports cleanly and then dies on the first call. The llm/ package imports only classify_backpressure from llm_scripting_kit.completion.halt, lazily, first shipped in 0.61.0, which is the min_version of the llm-scripting-kit entry; the edge is DEGRADE (llm/platform.py::_backpressure_classifier), so an absent or too-old lib warns with distinct messages and the gate falls back to exponential backoff. HaltError.retry_after_s is read with getattr and HALT_BACKPRESSURE is a local mirror, so neither is an import. A shared lib does not carry its own shared-lib edges to a consumer -- each venv declares what it needs. Edge to bootstrap_lib.claudx, class REFUSE. Under a claudx session (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_TEST set, the maintainer test harness) ClaudeCli.launch_bg and ClaudeCli.respawn probe refuse_supervised lazily and refuse loudly, because a supervised claude --bg session is not made to load the plugins under test; the refusal names an absent bootstrap_lib (claude plugin install bootstrap@plugins-kit) and a bootstrap_lib that lacks the claudx module or the symbol (claude plugin update bootstrap@plugins-kit) in distinct messages, each naming bootstrap >= 0.154.1, before any process starts. The artifact stays true because a claudx result is read as produced by the plugins under test, which an uncontained child would falsify, so nothing is produced instead. Outside claudx the module is never imported and no call is made on any consumer path, so the edge adds no requires_bootstrap floor (nested claude children, engine-internals.md). The claude -p backend reaches the same module through llm_scripting_kit.
